title: Choosing your own subjects
instructionsHu: Vitatkozz a vizsgáztatóval az alábbi állításról. A kiosztott álláspontod: az állítás MELLETT érvelsz – ezt az álláspontot a vita során nem változtathatod meg. Fejtsd ki az érveidet, reagálj a vizsgáztató ellenérveire, és próbáld meggyőzni őt.

debate.statement: Secondary school students should be allowed to choose all their subjects themselves
candidateIdeas: Students are more motivated when they study what they are interested in.
By the age of 15 or 16, many students know what they want to study at university.
Fewer compulsory subjects would mean less stress and more time for deeper learning.
Several successful education systems already give students a lot of choice.
Choosing their own subjects teaches students responsibility and decision-making.
examinerArguments: Teenagers often change their minds, and early choices may limit their options later.
Everyone needs a general education, including maths, history and science.
Students might choose the easiest subjects instead of the most useful ones.
Some subjects seem boring at first but become interesting later.
Schools could not organise timetables and teachers if every student chose freely.

followUpQuestions: But at fifteen, how can anyone know what they will need later in life?
Wouldn't many students simply choose the easiest subjects?
Don't you think everyone needs to know some history and science, whatever their plans?

usefulPhrases.hu: Meg kell bízni a diákokban, hogy ...

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Let's talk about this statement: 'Secondary school students should be allowed to choose all their subjects themselves.' What do you think?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I'm all for it. Students are far more motivated when they study what they're genuinely interested in. By the age of fifteen or sixteen, many of us already know roughly what we want to study at university – I'm planning to do medicine, for instance, so I'd love to spend more time on biology and chemistry. Fewer compulsory subjects would also mean less stress and more time for deeper learning.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: But at fifteen, how can anyone know what they will need later in life?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: That's true for some people, I admit – teenagers do change their minds. But choosing your subjects doesn't mean you're locked in forever; you could change your choices after a year. And making these decisions teaches responsibility, which we'll need anyway.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Wouldn't many students simply choose the easiest subjects?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Some might, but I think most students are more sensible than adults assume. Besides, university entrance requirements would still guide us: if you want to study engineering, you can't avoid maths and physics.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Don't you think everyone needs to know some history and science, whatever their plans?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I partly agree. Perhaps a compromise would be a small common core, including some history and science, in the first two years, and complete freedom of choice after that. That way, everyone would get a general education without being forced to study subjects they'll never use again.

notes: Feladat teljesítése: a vizsgázó következetesen a szabad tárgyválasztás mellett érvel (motiváció, pályaválasztás, kevesebb stressz, felelősségvállalás), saját példát hoz (orvosi egyetem), az ellenérveket részben elfogadja, majd cáfolja, a végén pedig konkrét kompromisszumot javasol (közös alaptárgyak az első két évben).

Szókincs: a vitához illő fordulatok (I'm all for it, That's true for some people, I admit, I partly agree, Perhaps a compromise would be) és pontos oktatási szavak (compulsory subjects, entrance requirements, common core).

Nyelvhelyesség: változatos szerkezetek hibátlanul – 'doesn't mean you're locked in', feltételes mód (would mean, would get), 'if you want to …, you can't avoid …' és a szenvedő igeneves 'without being forced to'.
Érdemes megtanulni: „I'm all for it”, „you're locked in forever”, „more sensible than adults assume”, „without being forced to”.
